govdocs-archive_org-PhysicalControlOfThe: José Delgado’s mind-taming book — toward a tamed mankind — tells of his bull-stopping wire work. The Yale brain man’s trials raised a storm in the 1960s. The book is a landmark of brain-lore and its rows. Its meaning still stings.
govdocs-archive_org-TheFirstHolocaust-Je: Heddesheimer’s First Holocaust — on old fund-drives crying six million lost ere 1914 — tells the other-side tale. The book fits the hot-history shelf. Its sayings are hotly fought over. Read it with both eyes open. Set it by the standard tales.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Preparation-Ear: This editorial — Watergate: An End Is in Sight?, creator unknown — is a press piece. The scandal’s end was near. The editorial hoped. The end came in August. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrogio-fopp: This 1913 reference article on Ambrogio Foppa — Caradosso, the goldsmith of the Renaissance. George Williamson praises his medals. His plaquettes graced the princely courts. Milan's mint knew his dies. A master of small wonders. His medals portray the Sforza dukes. His touch was sure and delicate.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arequipa: This 1913 reference piece on Arequipa — the Peruvian archdiocese of the white city. The entry tells its Andean story. Its cathedral faces the volcano's cone. The sillar stone glows in the sun. A highland see of the south. Its Santa Catalina convent charms visitors.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-atahuallpa: This 1913 reference piece on Atahualpa — the last Inca emperor. Adolph Bandelier tells his tragic fate. Pizarro seized him at Cajamarca. His ransom filled a room with gold. The fall of the Inca sun. His death ended the Inca line. His capture stunned the Andean world.
